title: Roy Fielding's REST Dissertation (2000)
explainer: The term REST, along with its defining constraints like statelessness and a uniform interface, comes from Roy Fielding's 2000 PhD dissertation, 'Architectural Styles and the Design of Network-based Software Architectures,' written at UC Irvine. Fielding had co-authored the HTTP and URI specifications himself, so REST was less a brand-new invention than his attempt to name and justify the architectural style the Web had already grown into. Knowing this origin clarifies why REST is a set of constraints describing how to use HTTP well, not a protocol or format you must follow to the letter.
